Vādirāja
(A. D. 1480-1600)
------------------------------------------
Vādirāja or वादिराज-tīrtha is one of the brightest स्तर्स् among the saṁnyāsins of the Mādhva tradition. He was a monk par excellence, a gigantic intellect and a योगि of the highest order endowed with supernatural psychic powers. He was the first to enter the बृन्दावन while still living. (See also RĀGHAVENDRA-TĪRTHA.)
He was the head of the Svādī or Sode मठ, one of the eight Maṭhas (pontifical seats) established by Madhvā-cārya (A. D. 1238-1317). He lived for 120 years.
He was born as the first son of Rāmabhaṭṭa and Gaurīdevī at Hūvinakere, a small village in the South Canara district of Karnataka State in A. D. 1480.
He practically grew up in the monastery (Sode मठ) under the loving care of its then pontiff, Vāgīśa who also educated him in all branches of learning necessary for a spiritual teacher.
He was later initiated into the monastic life with the new name वादिराज-tīrtha. In course of time he succeeded his गुरु Vāgīśa, to the pontifical seat.
His achievements as the pontiff of the Sode मठ and as a spiritual teacher are very impressive. He reorganised the paryāya system—taking turns for the worship of श्रीकृष्ण at the उडुपि temple—from that of two months to that of two years. He toured the country several times to spread the doctrines of द्वैत Vedānta as also the cult of devotion to विष्णु. He wrote several scholarly works in support of the द्वैत Vedānta philosophy such as Gururājīya-sudhā-ṭippaṇi, Tātparya-nirṇayaṭīkā, Yuktimallikā, Bhagavadgītā-ṭippaṇi and Tantrasāraṭīkā in Sanskrit. His treatises in Kannada are: Kannaḍa-tātparya nirṇaya and Bhramaragītā.
He also composed several devotional songs in the Kannaḍa language and continued the tradition of singing them in the Mādhva monasteries.
He was a devoted worshipper of हयग्रीव (an aspect of विष्णु) and had attained great yogic powers which he often used for the benefit of the devotees and the supplicants.
He was a junior contemporary of व्यासतीर्थ or Vyāsarāya (A. D. 1447-1539)—another great scholarly saint—under whom he was trained in the Vedāntic scriptures for some time.
Though his main seat of pontificate was at उडुपि, he chose to leave the body at Sode (in the North Canara district of Karnataka) itself. He entered into the बृन्दावन on the Phālguna-tṛtīyā day (during February /March) in A. D. 1600 and passed away.

vāda
(‘discussion’)
------------------------------------------
The word वाद is a technical term used by the न्याय philosophy (vide Nyāyasūtras (1.2.1). It means discussion and is अदोप्तिओन् of one of the two opposing sides. It is conducted according to logical rules and aims only at finding out the truth.
In it, both the vādī (exponent) and the pravtivādī (opponent) try to establish their own positions and refute that of the other with लोगिच्, quotations from authoritative sources and answering objections. This is very well illustrated by a philosophical discussion between the teacher and his student.
However, during the middle-ages, वाद or disputation among scholars to establish their supremacy was very common.
